status_summary: DoD directed on 2025-02-07 that contracting officers not use project labor agreements on large-scale construction, the VA issued similar guidance on 2025-02-20, and GSA issued a class exception for land port of entry projects on 2025-02-12 (memorandum SPE-2025-05). On 2025-05-16 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia preliminarily enjoined the DoD and GSA memoranda in North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense; a litigation clearinghouse reports the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case on 2025-07-07. OMB Memorandum M-25-29 of 2025-06-12 stated that Executive Order 14063 remains in effect, that blanket deviations are precluded and earlier deviations should be rescinded, and that the administration supports project labor agreements when practicable and cost effective, while widening the cost and competition exceptions. An August 2026 CRS In Focus describes the order and its FAR rule as still in place, so the operative policy keeps the requirement the Mandate's alternative view would end. No Davis-Bacon repeal action was found.

timeline.event: A DoD memorandum from the Office of the Secretary of Defense, signed by the principal director of contracting, directs contracting officers to stop using project labor agreements on large-scale construction projects, effective immediately, and to amend solicitations to remove them (as described by The Daily Reporter on 2025-02-13).
timeline.source: The Daily Reporter; Economic Policy Institute

timeline.event: GSA's Senior Procurement Executive issues memorandum SPE-2025-05, a class exception from the FAR 22.503(b) project labor agreement requirement for large-scale land port of entry construction projects, effective immediately until rescinded, citing urgency tied to border security and limited competition.

The VA issues guidance to all its procurement officers that contracting officers shall not use project labor agreements on large-scale construction projects and must amend solicitations, citing the Court of Federal Claims ruling of 2025-01-21 in MVL USA v. United States (ENR).

Judge Rudolph Contreras of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia grants a preliminary injunction against the DoD and GSA memoranda in North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense (No. 1:25-cv-01070), finding the unions likely to show the memoranda are not in accordance with law under the Administrative Procedure Act (Bloomberg Law).

OMB Memorandum M-25-29 stated that Executive Order 14063 remains in effect, that blanket deviations prohibiting project labor agreements are precluded and earlier deviations should be rescinded, and revised the cost and competition exceptions.

Plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense (No. 1:25-cv-01070, D.D.C.), and the case was closed, per a litigation clearinghouse summary; the docket was not opened.

title: End mandatory project labor agreement requirements on federal construction
uncertainties: The court order, the docket, the DoD memorandum and the VA instrument were not opened (the court docket host refuses automated fetches); the GSA class exception memorandum SPE-2025-05 of 2025-02-12 was opened on gsa.gov; the DoD memorandum of 2025-02-07 rests on a Daily Reporter article describing it, which does not call it a class deviation, and on an Economic Policy Institute account; the VA guidance of 2025-02-20 rests on an ENR report, which calls it guidance and does not name the instrument (a trade association's item calling it a class deviation is a lead only); the injunction rests on Bloomberg Law, Economic Policy Institute and Government Executive accounts, which agree; and the dismissal rests on a litigation clearinghouse summary, whose outcome field oddly lists the defendants as prevailing. A VA acquisition policy page (Flash 25-04, displayed date 2026-03-04) rescinds an earlier class deviation (Flash 25-03) citing the Court of Federal Claims decision; its relation to the 2025-02-20 guidance was not established. The CRS In Focus of 2026-08-12 (date from its file name) does not discuss the 2025 agency actions; it reports a separate Eleventh Circuit challenge to the order, affirmed against the challengers in April 2026 and pending on a rehearing petition. A September 2026 FAR overhaul proposal (parts 14, 28, 36 and 52) was read in part by the researcher and no project labor agreement text was found, but truncated Part 36 text means a change there is not ruled out. Diverged rather than blocked is a rubric judgment: the widened exceptions in M-25-29 may reduce project labor agreement use in practice, which could be read as limited movement toward the recommendation. The Mandate presents this item as an alternative view, so alignment is partial.
